raw_response:
I am old now, sixty-seven years, and I have grown sorghum on this small piece of land for many seasons. Sorghum does not ask for much — it is not like maize that cries for fertilizer. I have no money to buy the fertilizer bag, and here in Nsanje the rains are not reliable, so I will not waste my little kwacha on chemicals that may burn if the rain fails. I keep my own seed from last harvest like my father did, I put the small manure from my chickens and goats on the plot, and I work it myself with my wife — no money to pay anyone.
